chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from one of his companions, from Muthanna ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about an orphan who has recited the Quran, and there is nothing wrong with his intellect, and he has wealth in the hands of a man. So the man who holds the wealth wanted to do business with the orphan's wealth on a profit-sharing basis (mudarabah). So the boy permitted him in that. He (the Imam) said: 'It is not correct that he works with it until he reaches puberty (ihtilam) and hands over his wealth to him.' He said: 'And if he were to reach puberty and there was not intellect for him, nothing would be handed over to him ever.'
Humayd, from al-Hasan, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), similar to that.
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for an orphan to take possession of their wealth in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the Shia juristic distinction between biological maturity (bulugh) and financial competence (rushd), establishing that puberty alone does not grant an orphan full control over their wealth. It highlights that even if an orphan is physically mature, a lack of sound intellect (aql) or guidance prevents the transfer of assets, ensuring their financial protection until they demonstrate sufficient discernment to manage their estate.
